newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan current account surplus on falling trend-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan current account surplus on falling trend-MOF.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus is on a declining trend, a Finance Ministry official told a news conference on Monday.
"Both the current account figures for December and 1996 have declined and that trend should continue for some time," the official said.
He said the rise in imports had been larger than that of exports and, along with an increase in the services deficit, was likely to keep the overall current account surplus on a declining trend.
The official also said the trade surplus continued to be on a declining track.

The Finance Ministry announced earlier on Monday that the surplus in Japan's current account shrank 23.1 percent to 820.7 billion yen in December from a year earlier, while the current account surplus for 1996 also shrank 30.9 percent from a year earlier to 7.1806 trillion yen.
